To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount of myocardial salvage, the improvement in left ventricular function, and the mortality rate are determined by the time to reperfusion and the adequacy (or degree) of the reperfusion.

(i) the time to reperfusion and the adequacy with which reflow occurs are the two most important determinants of functional recovery; (ii) the amount of myocardial salvage, the recovery of regional function, the reduction in left ventricular volume, and the improvement in global left ventricular function all correlate with the reduction in mortality; (iii) the time to thrombolysis is a more important determinant of functional recovery than the method used to achieve thrombolysis; (iv

the amount of myocardial salvage, the recovery of ventricular systolic function, and the reduction in the incidence of congestive heart failure and sudden cardiac death after reperfusion are directly related to the time delay until successful reperfusion is obtained and to the adequacy of reperfusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of reflow on left ventricular recovery.
the mechanisms of reperfusion and the factors that determine the amount of myocardial salvage and the recovery of left-ventricular function after reperfusion.
the mechanisms that lead to recovery of left ventricle function following thrombolytic treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reperfusion is the most important factor in determining the amount and quality of salvaged myocardium.
thrombolytic treatment of acute myocardial infarcion improves left ventricular function, salvages myocardium and reduces mortality.
the recovery of myocardial function is the most important mechanism for enhancing survival after reperfusion therapy in acute myocardinal infarction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the recovery of left-ventricular function is dependent on the time delay until the reperfusion, the adequacy of reflow, the underlying coronary artery anatomy and the method of measurement used to assess the recovery of function.
the most important determinant of the effect of thrombolylic therapy in acute myocardium infarction is the time delay until the onset of reperfusion.
thrombolysis is a safe and effective therapy for patients with acute myocardial infraction and that reperfusion is associated with a significant enhancement of survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of myocardial salvage and functional recovery is related to the time delay until coronary reperfusion is obtained.
the time from the start of symptoms to the start of treatment is the single most important factor in determining whether a patient will benefit from thrombolytic treatment.
the time to treatment and the degree of myocardial salvage are critical determinants of the recovery of ventricular dysfunction and survival.
